scenes.title: Different expertise. One patient.
scenes.visual: An illustrated meeting room surrounds the real central wall. Move towards the synthetic case; source records orbit the clinicians.

cues.text: This is a multidisciplinary tumour board. Different specialists, bringing their expertise to one patient's care.
Before they can agree a plan, they must bring the scans, pathology, treatment history and evidence together.

scenes.title: A specialist. An agent. A shared task.
scenes.visual: Move from the oncologist to the actual oncology desk. Reveal separately labelled human and agent pairs; open the real radiology and pathology desks.

cues.text: MDT Observatory explores a different way to prepare. Each specialist has a role-specific agent.
The oncology agent reviews treatment. Radiology examines imaging. Pathology brings the tissue findings.
The agent represents a professional perspective. The specialist steers the work and remains responsible for clinical judgement.

scenes.title: What makes an agent useful?
scenes.visual: Expand an agent into model, permitted tools and role/context layers. Follow evidence from the actual application drawer back into the role workspace.

cues.text: A model interprets information and communicates. Tools retrieve the records and evidence the role is allowed to use.
Its role and case context focus the work. These are curated sources, with access limits visible.
This film shows the application's scripted rehearsal, not live model inference.

scenes.title: One case. Different working views.
scenes.visual: Editorial match cuts between real imaging, pathology, oncology, surgical and chair screens; keep the patient context visible.

cues.text: Everyone sees the same case. Their working views are different.
Imaging and tissue findings. Treatment and surgery.
The chair sees the shared questions and where the specialties disagree.

scenes.title: Find the question that matters.
scenes.visual: Concise editorial paraphrases of public positions flow across the real workspace wall. An unresolved question forms at their intersection.

cues.text: The agents publish positions into a shared meeting. The chair coordinates the unresolved questions.
In this synthetic case, treatment has reduced the liver disease. But response alone does not settle the next step.
Can every original liver site be addressed? What does the small, indeterminate lung nodule mean?
And how well does the evidence support this particular sequence of treatment? Those questions need attention.

scenes.title: Bring in human judgement.
scenes.visual: Highlight real unresolved friction; connect the radiology agent to its clinician, show typed guidance, and return to the updated position.

cues.text: When evidence is incomplete, the uncertainty stays visible. The system asks for specialist input.
Here, the radiologist asks for review of all nine liver sites, vessel margins and the lung nodule.
That guidance returns to the discussion. Remaining conditions stay attached.

scenes.title: Review the plan. Preserve the conditions.
scenes.visual: Show the real conditional proposal, changing version-bound concurrence states, and captured decision. Distinguish clinician review from automatic demo-policy support.

cues.text: A conditional plan now comes back for review. Required human concurrence is tied to this exact version.
The aim is less time assembling facts, and more time on judgement. Agreement does not remove uncertainty.

scenes.title: Carry the decision into care.
scenes.visual: Begin with the real outcome, actions and visible document-drafting failure. Branch into labelled editorial letter illustrations; transform a short patient excerpt from English to German.

cues.text: The recorded outcome carries the actions, conditions and review history forward.
With a model connected, it can draft a colleague letter and a patient summary for named clinician approval.
Drafting is unavailable in this local run. These illustrated excerpts show the intended communication.
Plain language. The patient's language. Always reviewed before sharing.

scenes.title: More time for clinical judgement.
scenes.visual: Return to the humans in the meeting room, agents quietly beside them, and the captured decision on the wall. Hold a restrained blue-and-white end title.

cues.text: Let the agents prepare, search, compare and coordinate.
Give specialists more time for the difficult questions, the patient's priorities, and the judgement that remains theirs.
